# Copilot instructions

`AGENTS.md` contains the shared Laravel and project rules; follow it alongside these repository-specific notes.

## Build, test, and lint

- Run the full PHPUnit suite with `composer test` or `php artisan test --compact`.
- Run one test file with `php artisan test --compact tests\Feature\BookingTest.php`.
- Run one test method with `php artisan test --compact tests\Feature\BookingTest.php --filter=test_name`.
- Format changed PHP files with `vendor\bin\pint --dirty --format agent`.
- Run static analysis with `vendor\bin\phpstan analyse`.
- Build frontend assets with `npm run build`; use `npm run dev` for Vite or `composer run dev` for the full local stack.
- PHPUnit uses an in-memory SQLite database. Feature tests inherit `RefreshDatabase` and the base test case's admin/OTP session setup.

## Architecture

- This is a Laravel 13 / PHP 8.5 application. `bootstrap\app.php` mounts `routes\admin.php` under `/admin` with authentication, two-factor, and forced-password-change middleware; `routes\web.php` holds the frontend and account flows.
- The main domain is users, vehicles, and bookings. Eloquent models and relationships live in `app\Models`; HTTP controllers coordinate workflows and use Form Requests for validation and authorization. Focused reusable logic lives in `app\Services` and `app\Support`.
- Admin pages are Blade views using the Bootstrap 5 `layouts.xpress` layout. Interactive user, vehicle, and booking lists are Livewire PowerGrid components in `app\Livewire\Admin`; their components own table search/filter, export, and bulk actions.
- `AppServiceProvider` defines the central role-based Gates. Admin routes add entity-level `can` middleware, and controllers/Livewire actions also authorize sensitive operations.
- Core models use Spatie Activitylog and deleted-model tracking. Spreadsheet import/export safety is centralized in `App\Support\Spreadsheet`; preserve its formula-neutralization behavior at spreadsheet boundaries.

## Repository-specific conventions

- Keep route names and route organization consistent with the existing `xpress.*` routes. Continue using Form Requests for endpoint input and the existing Gate checks for authorization.
- Keep multi-record writes transactional. Booking codes are generated by the `Booking` model from a locked sequence; do not accept caller-supplied booking codes.
- Build admin data tables with the existing Livewire PowerGrid pattern. Bulk actions must validate selected IDs and authorize each affected model, not just the table or request.
- Preserve model activity logging, deleted-model tracking, and existing foreign-key deletion behavior when changing CRUD flows. Avoid adding manual activity entries that duplicate model-event logs.
- Use `layouts.xpress`, existing Blade components, Bootstrap, and Select2 for admin UI changes.
- For a new CRUD module, follow `.opencode/skills/biker-crud-module/`: inspect the closest existing module, present the implementation plan, and wait for explicit approval before coding.
- After code changes, refresh the repository knowledge graph with `graphify update .`.
